questions.question: Why did English keep Anglo-Saxon words for animals (cow, pig) but French words for their meat (beef, pork)?
options: Anglo-Saxon peasants raised the animals while French-speaking nobles ate the meat
The Church required French food words
questions.explanation: After the Norman Conquest, the peasants who raised animals spoke English while the nobles who dined on them spoke French.

questions.question: What happened in 1066?
options: The founding of the British Empire
The union of England and Scotland
questions.explanation: In 1066 William of Normandy conquered England, bringing French language and culture to the ruling class.

questions.question: When did the Industrial Revolution take place in Britain?
questions.explanation: The Industrial Revolution (c. 1760-1840) transformed Britain's economy and society.

questions.question: What was the "double edge" of the Industrial Revolution?
options: It created wealth and technology but also slums, child labour and pollution
questions.explanation: Alongside higher wages and new technology came slums, child labour, pollution and dramatic differences in life expectancy.

questions.question: Which period came first in British history?
questions.explanation: Roman Britain (43-410 AD) preceded Anglo-Saxon England, the Norman Conquest, the Tudors and the Victorians.
